verdict: Guests paid more per room — RevPAR rose 8.8% — but with last year's big asset-sale gains gone, GAAP net income fell by more than half to $71M.

segments.name: Rooms
segments.note: Room rentals across Host's 73 comparable hotels (about 41,000 rooms), helped by World Cup travel and stronger business demand.

segments.name: Food & beverage
segments.note: Restaurants, bars, banquets and events at the hotels.

segments.name: Other hotel revenue
segments.note: Parking, resort fees, spa and other on-property spending.

segments.name: Condominium sales
segments.note: Sales of condo units being developed next to the Four Seasons Resort Orlando.

opex.name: Management fees
opex.note: Fees paid to the hotel brands (Marriott, Hyatt and others) that run Host's hotels day to day.

opex.name: Other property-level expenses
opex.note: Property taxes, insurance, utilities and other costs of owning the hotel buildings.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear-and-tear charge on hotel buildings and renovations — a non-cash cost, and the big reason GAAP profit looks low for a REIT.

opex.name: Corporate & other
opex.note: Head-office costs: general and administrative spending plus stock-based pay.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $59M, partly offset by $17M of interest income and $5M of equity earnings from affiliates, plus $6M of other losses — a year ago this line held $122M of gains, mostly from asset sales.
follow100Note: For a hotel REIT, the cash story sits in funds from operations (FFO), which adds back the $187M depreciation charge: NAREIT FFO was $261M ($0.38 per share) and Adjusted FFO was $268M ($0.39 per share) — both up about 11-12% on a per-share basis. Net income attributable to Host Inc. was $70M after $1M belonging to non-controlling interests. Direct costs here combine rooms, food-and-beverage and other departmental expenses ($853M) with the $6M cost of condos sold.

takeaways.title: Rates carried the hotels
takeaways.text: Comparable RevPAR rose 8.8% to $219.50 — room rates up 5.7% and occupancy up 2.1 points — and Total RevPAR rose 7.3% as food and beverage spending grew.

takeaways.title: Hotel-level profit rose 11%
takeaways.text: Comparable hotel EBITDA reached $331M with a 25.2% margin, up 0.9 points, as higher room rates outran wage increases.

takeaways.title: The profit drop is a missing gain
takeaways.text: Net income fell from $163M to $71M almost entirely because last year included $122M of other gains, mostly asset sales; this year that line was a $6M loss. Operating profit actually rose 20% to $121M.

oneTimers: Other gains swung from +$122M a year ago to -$6M — asset-sale gains that did not repeat are the whole story of the net income decline.
After quarter-end Host bought two hotels — 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge ($202M) and Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West ($172M) — and raised full-year RevPAR growth guidance to about 6.75%.
